Arrays
An n-element array, or n-array A[1..n] is a 1D data structure (DS)
whose elements (keys) are referenced by their index A[i],1 <i<n.
An array is usually stored in the computer’s DRAM contiguously.
Its usage is shown for a sorting problem where a number sequence
aj, 1<i<n, needs to be permuted to a;’, 1 <i<n,s+t.a;’ <a,’,
i<j.
An algorithm called insertion sort permutes A[1..n] s.t. upon
termination A[i] < A[j], 1<i<j<n.

Runtime Analysis
The runtime T(n) relates to the input size which for A[1..n] is n.
Reference A[i] to RAM takes constant time, independently of n.
Constant time is charged to code line unless it calls function.
Counting number of times each line is executed yields runtime
dependence on n.
Of interests are worst-case and average-case runtime, where average
is usually more difficult to derive than worst.
March 2022 Algorithms and DS |: Elementary DS 5

Worst-case input analysis result bounds the runtime of any input.
Average-case is more difficult. Requires knowledge of the input
probabilistic nature, and applying probabilistic analysis.
What is the worst-case input instance of INSERTION—SORT ? (HW)
Worst-case INSERTION—SORT runtimw is quadratic in n. (HW)
The algorithms in this course are deterministic, where different runs
for same input yield same runtime.
Randomized algorithms are left for advanced courses.

Queues

INSERT called ENQUEUE, DELETE is called DEQUEUE. (code CLRS 10.1)

Heap Sort
Some applications require to remove the largest (smallest) key from the
heap and then recover the heap property of the reminder n — 1 keys.
HEAP-EXTRACT-MAX(A)
max = A[l] // largest key is the 1%
A[1l] = A[A.heap-size] // fillin the vacant location
A.heap-size = A.heap-size — 1 // decrease heap size
MAX-HEAPIFY (A, 1) // recover heap property
return max
Heap Sort (J.W.J. Williams 1964) applies n — 1 HEAP—EXTRACT—MAX
(MIN) repetitions to sort an n-array in decreasing (increasing) order.
(HW: write code and prove O(nlog n) runtime.)
